# tsuru_platform (Resource)

Manages a tsuru platform. Note: the tsuru API does not return the Dockerfile content back, so it cannot be refreshed from the API; terraform will keep whatever value is set in the configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "tsuru_platform" "python" {
  name     = "python"
  disabled = false
  dockerfile = <<-EOT
    FROM tsuru/python:latest
    EOT
}

# `image` is a convenience alternative to `dockerfile`: it generates a
# Dockerfile with a single `FROM ${image}` instruction. `image` and
# `dockerfile` are mutually exclusive.
resource "tsuru_platform" "nodejs" {
  name  = "nodejs"
  image = "tsuru/nodejs:latest"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Platform name

### Optional

- `disabled` (Boolean) Whether the platform is disabled, preventing new apps from being created with it
- `dockerfile` (String) Content of the Dockerfile used to build the platform image. Required to create the platform and whenever a new image build is needed.
- `image` (String) Base image to build the platform from. This is a convenience alternative to `dockerfile`: it generates a Dockerfile with a single `FROM ${image}` instruction.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `update_trigger` (String) Arbitrary value that, when changed, forces the platform image to be rebuilt from the current dockerfile content without requiring any other field to change

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `images` (List of String) List of images built for this platform

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String)
- `delete` (String)
- `update` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import tsuru_platform.resource_name "name"

# example
terraform import tsuru_platform.python "python"
```
